facts.statement: The fossil of Houornis was discovered in 1993 by Zhou Zhonghe near Boluochi in Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: The specimen was found in 1993 by Zhou Zhonghe near the town of Boluochi in Liaoning Province, China.

facts.statement: Houornis is known only from fossil impressions rather than preserved bones.
facts.quote: The actual bones of this specimen were not preserved, but rather can be seen by the impressions they left in the surrounding rock.

facts.statement: Houornis caudatus was a small bird with an elongated, toothy snout and perching feet.
facts.quote: Houornis caudatus was a small enantiornithean with a slightly elongated, toothy snout and perching feet.

facts.statement: Houornis possessed an unusually long pygostyle, a structure made of fused tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: It does appear to have an unusually long pygostyle (a component of the tail made of fused vertebrae).

facts.statement: The species was originally named Cathayornis caudatus in 1997 based on a mistaken belief that it had a long bony tail.
facts.quote: It was originally thought to have a relatively long, bony tail intermediate in length between modern birds and long-tailed birds like Archaeopteryx, and so was in 1997 by Hou Lianhu given the name Cathayornis caudatus, meaning "tailed Cathay bird".

facts.statement: Houornis lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Houornis caudatus was previously classified as a species of Cathayornis and was once considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: It is known from a single species, Houornis caudatus, which had been once been classified as a species of Cathayornis, and has also been regarded as a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Some researchers consider Houornis dubious due to the poor preservation and incomplete nature of the fossil.
facts.quote: While some researchers have considered the species dubious due to the poor preservation quality and incomplete nature of the fossil

facts.statement: A specimen referred to the species in 1997 was confirmed as Houornis in 2015.
facts.quote: Specimen IVPP V10533, the rear of a skeleton, had in 1997 been referred to the species by Hou and this was confirmed in 2015.

rejected.statement: In 2015, Wang Min and Liu Di assigned the species to its own genus, Houornis, after comparing it to similar species.
rejected.quote: a 2015 study by Wang Min and Liu Di was complete enough to be compared to similar species... and so they assigned it to its own genus, Houornis
rejected.reason: quote not found verbatim in the source

rejected.statement: Wang and Liu (2015) classified Houornis as incertae sedis because they could not determine its relationships with other members of Enantiornithes.
rejected.quote: They placed Houornis as incertae sedis.
